title: Cooperative Kernel Waveform Orchestration Spec
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This spec describes the Cooperative Kernel Waveform Orchestration (CKWO) design: a scheduling abstraction and operational playbook for coordinating short-lived inference kernels across heterogeneous GPU pools to reduce tail latency and improve packing efficiency while preserving isolation guarantees. CKWO is intended for the high-concurrency, mixed-model workloads that characterize Redwood’s hosted API and Dedicated clusters.

Goals
-----
- Reduce 95th/99th percentile token-generation latency by coordinating micro-batches across kernels.
- Improve kernel packing to reduce per-token GPU cycles without increasing head-of-line blocking.
- Make kernel coordination observable and debuggable with explicit wave metadata.
- Provide safe degradation modes that never violate customer SLOs (latency/COST isolation).

Scope and non-goals
-------------------
- In-scope: inter-kernel coordination for attention/matmul kernels, batching signals, KV-cache-aware warmup, and telemetry annotations for wave events.
- Out-of-scope: model architecture changes, driver-level preemption, and tenant-level admission control policy (higher-level quota layer handles admission).

Conceptual overview
-------------------
CKWO organizes short-lived kernel executions into "waves". A wave is a logical grouping of kernels that can be co-scheduled with cooperative guarantees:
- Wave phases: PREPARE -> PACK -> EXECUTE -> COMMIT -> CLEANUP.
- Each wave carries a Wave ID (UUID), priority class (low/normal/high), and waveform hints (expected sequence length, kv-cache affinity, quantization tag).
- Waves may be single-tenant or multi-tenant depending on affinity and isolation constraints.

Architecture components
-----------------------
- Wave Controller (service): creates and coordinates waves per GPU node. Runs in the runtime control plane.
- Kernel Coordinator (in-runtime agent): local to each GPU process, executes the waveform phases and enforces packing and fairness.
- Wave Metadata Bus (lightweight pub/sub): transports wave lifecycle events (wave-start, pack-complete, exec-complete) to telemetry and tracing.
- Admission shim: lightweight hook at request enqueue time that emits waveform hints and SLO tags.

Scheduling primitives and contracts
---------------------------------
1. Slot promises: a kernel can promise a time-limited slot to the wave controller when it has partial readiness (e.g., token prefix loaded). The promise includes expected slot duration and token budget.
2. Cooperative preemption token: short consensus token to allow higher-priority waves to reclaim unused slots during PACK phase (fast-path only).
3. Quiesce boundary: kernels must implement a quiesce handler to checkpoint the KV cache pointer and return consistent partial outputs on preemption.

Wave orchestration lifecycle (detailed)
-------------------------------------
1) PREPARE
   - Admission shim validates hints and annotates the request.
   - Wave Controller assigns preliminary Wave ID and target node(s) based on affinity and SLOs.
   - Telemetry: emit wave.prep.{wave_id}.
2) PACK
   - Kernel Coordinator gathers ready kernels and evaluates pack candidates using waveform hint heuristics.
   - Pack decision includes which kernels will run together and estimated duration.
   - Telemetry: emit wave.pack.{wave_id} with pack composition and estimated duration.
3) EXECUTE
   - Kernels execute with coordinated start. Micro-batching may be performed only if all kernels meet packing constraints.
   - Cooperative preemption may be triggered if a higher-priority wave claims slots.
   - Telemetry: wave.exec.{wave_id} including per-kernel timing and kernel IDs.
4) COMMIT
   - Outputs are merged, cache pointers advanced; per-tenant quotas updated.
5) CLEANUP
   - Memory and ephemeral allocations released; pack accounting updated.

Observability contract (what to emit)
------------------------------------
- Required events: wave.created, wave.pack_attempt, wave.pack_commit, wave.exec_start, wave.exec_end, wave.preempt_request, wave.preempt_granted, wave.cleanup_complete.
- Each event must include: wave_id, node_id, kernel_id(s), priority, estimated_duration_ms, actual_duration_ms, pack_reason (latency/cost/affinity), and a diagnostic tag.
- Correlate with existing traces: append wave_id to the request trace root.

Config knobs (table)
--------------------
| name | default | description | operator guidance |
| wave.max_pack_size | 8 | Max kernels in a single pack | Start at default, tune downward for high tail latency |
| wave.max_pack_latency_ms | 8 | Max time to wait while assembling a pack | Lower to prioritize latency; increase for better efficiency |
| wave.priority_strictness | medium | How strongly controller prefers higher-priority waves | Set to high for SLO-critical clusters |
| wave.coop_preempt_window_ms | 2 | Time window where cooperative preemption can be claimed during PACK | Keep small to minimize instability |
| wave.kv_affinity_threshold | 0.7 | Confidence threshold to colocate wave with warm KV cache | Use 0.8+ for latency-sensitive traffic |

Example pack decision pseudocode
-------------------------------
```
// simplified pack selection logic
candidates = gather_ready_kernels()
score(candidate) = affinity_score*0.6 + priority_score*0.3 - est_duration*0.1
selected = top_k(candidates, wave.max_pack_size, score)
if max_est_duration(selected) > wave.max_pack_latency_ms: fallback_to_singleton()
```

Safe degradation and fallbacks
------------------------------
- If pack assembly time exceeds wave.max_pack_latency_ms, controller falls back to executing available kernels immediately (singletons).
- If cooperative preemption fails repeatedly for >3 waves in 60s for a node, disable PACK on that node for 60s (circuit breaker).
- If observed 95th latency increases by >20% after a rollout, rollback the new controller and enable conservative packing config.

Runbook: investigating long PACK times
-------------------------------------
1. Alert triggers: packing_latency.node > 99th percentile threshold for 5m.
2. Triage steps:
   a) Query last 10 wave.pack_attempt events for the node: composition, estimated vs actual durations.
   b) Check node GPU utilization and dispatch queue lengths (node/gpu/{id}/utilization, dispatch.queue.length).
   c) Verify kv-cache hit ratio for packed kernels — low affinity increases waiting.
   d) If packing contention due to small kernels, reduce wave.max_pack_size or increase priority_strictness.
3. Mitigation:
   - Temporarily set wave.max_pack_latency_ms to 3ms for high-priority traffic.
   - Trigger node-level PACK-disable circuit breaker if pack attempts > 100 and mean wait > 15ms.
4. Postmortem: record root cause, pack composition, and correlate with traffic mix.

Benchmarks and validation strategy
---------------------------------
- Microbenchmarks: synthetic mixes of (short, medium, long) sequences at concurrencies [10, 50, 200] measuring p50/p95/p99 for token latency and per-token GPU cycles.
- A/B rollout: shadow CKWO with pack disabled for 24h; compare cost-per-token and tail latency. Staged rollout matrix described below.

Rollout plan and metrics
-----------------------
1) Canary (5% traffic, internal customers): run CKWO controller in parallel mode (no-enforce) for 48h. Monitor wave packing ratio and tail latency.
2) Limited (20%): enable CKWO with conservative knobs; monitor 1h and 24h windows.
3) Gradual (50% -> 100%): increase over days if both cost and latency show improvement or remain within 3% of baseline.

Key success metrics (track weekly)
- pack_efficiency_ratio: (tokens served under packs)/(tokens total) target > 0.35 after warmup.
- p95_token_latency change <= +3% during rollout.
- per_token_gpu_cycles delta <= -5% (cost savings target).

Telemetry dashboards and alerts (minimum)
- Wave overview: pack rate, average pack size, pack latency distribution.
- Node health: pack_attempts, pack_failures, preempt_requests/grants.
- Alerts: pack_latency.node.high, pack_preempt.failure_spike, wave.exec.error_rate.

Instrumentation examples
-----------------------
- Example Wave event JSON (annotate into existing trace):
{
  "event": "wave.pack_commit",
  "wave_id": "wf-2a7d9c1e",
  "node_id": "node-gpu-34",
  "kernels": ["k-124", "k-125"],
  "priority": "normal",
  "est_duration_ms": 4,
  "actual_duration_ms": 3
}

- Example runtime config snippet (YAML):
wave:
  max_pack_size: 6
  max_pack_latency_ms: 6
  priority_strictness: medium
  coop_preempt_window_ms: 2
  kv_affinity_threshold: 0.75

References and related work
---------------------------

Appendix: experiment checklist
-----------------------------
1. Prepare synthetic load generator with realistic prompt length distribution.
2. Baseline run (no CKWO) for 12h, record p50/p95/p99, cost.
3. Enable CKWO in no-enforce mode for 24h, compare signals.
4. Enable conservative CKWO config on a single node pool for 6h, validate correctness and tail behaviour.
5. Execute A/B run for 24h with 20% traffic, evaluate.

End of spec. For implementation RFC, see the kernel-and-scheduling team wiki space and open the design PR referenced in related_pages.
